6. **Burnet** <note>Thomas Burnet (c. 1635–1715), an English clergyman whose "Sacred Theory of the Earth" attempted to combine geology with the biblical narrative</note> presents the earth in seven specific forms: 1. waste and empty; 2. before the Great Flood; 3. during the Great Flood; 4. after the Great Flood; 5. in the conflagration <note>original: "Brand"; the fire expected to consume the world at the end of time</note>; 6. during the thousand years <note>the Millennium</note>; 7. after the judgment. Strictly speaking, there are only two states of the earth, as well as of heaven: the former and the new. The others, especially regarding the earth, are rapid transitions; and one should also add the state from the third day of the world's creation until the entrance of sin. Furthermore, the seven bowls <note>referring to the "bowls of God's wrath" in Revelation 16</note> bring a greater change to the earth than the thousand years do.

### XXI. 3. And — be their GOD

However, heaven and the new earth, as well as the lake of fire, are described in verses 5–8.

¶ **The dwelling**) This discourse has four parts: (1) Behold, the dwelling of **GOD** with **men**; (2) and He will dwell with them; (3) and they shall be His people; (4) and He Himself, **GOD** with them, will be their **GOD**. The first part is explained by the fourth, and the second by the third. There, the covenant between **GOD** and His people will reach its most glorious establishment <term>establishment; original: "Erection"; used here in the sense of the formal setting up or fulfillment of a legal/divine structure</term>. v. 7. **Ezek. XXXVII. 26. 27. 2 Cor. VI. 16. Heb. VIII. 10.**

2. It is a firmly established holy **residence-city**, and at the same time a dwelling or tabernacle, where **GOD** dwells among **men** in a familiar <term>familiar; original: "familiaire"; implying an intimate, family-like or close social relationship</term> manner.

¶ **With men**) That is: Now humans have been brought to the point where they are capable <note>original: "tüchtig"; meaning fit, prepared, or spiritually qualified</note> of having **GOD** dwelling among them. The little word "with" or "among" <note>original: "bey oder mit"; referring to the Greek preposition *meta* used in the phrase "with men"</note> occurs here three times.

2. It is not all the same whether it says **GOD** is with **men**, or they are with Him. **Chap. III. 20. John XVII. 12. 24.** And when it is stated so emphatically here that **GOD** is with **men**, it indicates His wondrous condescension <term>condescension; original: "Condescendenz"; in 18th-century theology, this refers to God’s voluntary act of "stepping down" from His infinite majesty to be present with finite creatures</term> and descent, as He stays with them and they, so to speak, become accustomed to Him. This dwelling He has prepared not for Himself, but for them. **Heb. XI. 16.**

...shall be his Father, just as the heavenly worshippers always address Him who sits upon the throne as their God, and not as their Father. <meta>This page continues the comparison between the vision of the New Jerusalem in Revelation 21 and the prophetic vision of the city found in the Book of Ezekiel. It explores the differences in their descriptions, timing, and architectural details.</meta>

<page-num>1000</page-num>
<header>XXI. 10. And—from God.</header>
<sig>J</sig>
<meta>catchword: Jerusalem</meta>

Jerusalem, as it existed before and after the Babylonian captivity <note>The historical period in the 6th century BCE when the Jewish people were exiled to Babylon.</note>, is distinct from the city described in Ezekiel and in the Book of Revelation. These two visions, however, do agree with each other in many details—as we shall observe from time to time—yet they are also different in even more respects. Ezekiel reports on the land and its new division outside the city; John, however, does not. The latter [John], on the other hand, mentions the twelve angels, the twelve apostles, the twelve precious stones, and the twelve pearls; but the former [Ezekiel] does not. The former [Ezekiel] describes the temple and the divine service within it very extensively, with frequent allusions to the Levitical <note>Referring to the laws and priestly duties of the tribe of Levi as established in the Old Testament.</note> regulations regarding sacrifices, etc.; but the latter [John] saw no temple and describes the city as truly glorious and heavenly, which also here—as we shall soon see—has a much different and larger measurement than in Ezekiel. It is true that in Ezekiel, Gog and Magog <note>Symbolic figures representing the enemies of God’s people who appear in apocalyptic literature.</note> also precede the holy city; however, the prophecy of the city begins with a completely new date. In both Ezekiel and John, it is the same Gog and Magog, but the city in Ezekiel appears much sooner, after the downfall of the Beast <note>A reference to the defeat of the Antichrist or the oppressive world power described earlier in Revelation.</note>, whereas in John it appears only after the Final Judgment. At that time, the former city is not demolished but is, as it were, clothed over by this one. Both prophecies can therefore be very well compared with one another, and one explained through the other.

<summary>This page compares the visions of the holy city in the books of Ezekiel and Revelation, noting their differences in timing, measurements, and architectural features like the temple. It concludes that while distinct, the two prophecies are meant to be studied together to understand the progression of the divine city.</summary>

III. **The measuring rods are angelic-human: the stadia, however, are human and common.**

One thing is human, another is angelic-human. The "number of the beast" <note>A reference to the number 666 from Revelation 13:18</note> is called human, while the measuring rods are called angelic-human: therefore, these rods are not merely human. The stadia, on the other hand, are not called angelic-human: thus they are, by virtue of the contrast, human or common. This same contrast is found in the 42 months of the beast compared to its human number; likewise in Daniel 9:24 and 10:2–3 in the Hebrew text, where "three weeks of days" <note>original: "שלושה שבועות ימים" (sheloshah shavuim yamim)</note> are contrasted against the "seventy weeks." These stadia are common units, just like the 1,600 stadia in Chapter 14:20. One cannot make them smaller; for the majesty of the divine way of speaking prefers to present something greater with lesser words, rather than something lesser with greater words, especially in matters of good things. Furthermore, no one will desire to make them larger here, for 12,000 stadia already provide a size that is difficult to believe. *Celestial Sphere* <note>original: "Himmels-Kugel"</note> page 180 (which, along with other passages of this treatise, are to be compared with my notes on this 21st Chapter), states that the 12,000 stadia <term>Stadien: ancient units of length, roughly 600 feet</term> and the 144 cubits <term>Ellen: cubits, usually the length of a forearm</term> or parts are a completely equal measure: and concerning this equality, the situation is as follows. (1) If one wishes to compare it to worldly architecture: at Ecbatana <note>An ancient city in Media, modern-day Iran</note>, the thickness of the wall relates to the height as 5 to 7 in the Greek <note>original: "Griechischen"</note> text of Judith 1, or as 3 to 7 in the Latin <note>original: "Lateinischen"</note> version; at Babylon, as 1 to 4; at Tangier, it relates as 2 to 5, and in part as 3 to 10; at Ahmedabad <note>original: "Amadabat"</note> in the East Indies, as 2 2/3 to 5. # And—is of an angel. XXI. 16. 17.

The city’s length and width, and thus a single measure, namely 12,000 stadia <term>stadia: ancient Greek units of length, approximately 600 feet or 1/8 of a mile</term>, are reported: similarly, for the wall, the size and height, and thus also a single measure, namely 144 measuring rods <term>rods: translated from "Meßruthen," a larger unit of measure often used for land, typically consisting of several cubits</term>, are reported, as we noted in the preceding proposition. Added to this now is that, just as those lengths and widths are equal to each other at 12,000 stadia, so too are this size and height equal to each other at 144 rods. Furthermore, by virtue of this latter equality, "size"—alongside height—cannot be understood as thickness (which would turn the city itself into a mere wall), and thus nothing else than the length of the wall on all four sides is meant, which simultaneously suggests the incomparable greatness of the city itself. The length of the wall, however, is certainly not less than the length of the city, as there is no suburb here; and the height of the wall is not greater than the height of the city, otherwise it would be a tower. Thus, by means of the height, which is the same for the city itself and its wall, all dimensions <term>dimensions: original Latin "dimensiones," referring to the measurable extents of the structure</term> for both together are made consistently equal; and so the 12,000 stadia and the 144 measuring rods are infallibly and entirely equal to one another.

No human could grasp what the 144 angelic-human <note>original: "englisch-menschliche." In this context, "englisch" refers to the nature of an angel (Engel), referencing Revelation 21:17: "according to the measure of a man, that is, of an angel."</note> measuring rods might be; but now, the 12,000 common stadia provide the indispensable key, found nowhere else.

# XXI 16. 17. And—it is of an Angel. [1015]

The fraction involving the stadia should not lead us astray, because the length of a stadium is not based on nature itself, but is determined by human convention <note>original: "menschlicher Willkühr"</note>, and the fraction eventually disappears so quickly and beautifully within the mathematical progression.

Through this divine method, it turns out quite fittingly that despite the equality of the city's length and height—a concept so unknown on earth—the prophetic description still aligns with common speech. This is because the city's length is expressed in stadia <term>stadia: an ancient Greek unit of distance, here used for the horizontal span</term>, as is customary in other city descriptions, while its height is captured in measuring rods <term>measuring rods: "Ruthen," a vertical or land-surveying unit used here to describe the city's height</term>.

### V. This City is Much Larger than the City in Ezekiel.

There are 46 ⅔ stadia to one German mile <note>original: "deutsche Meile"; a historical German unit of distance, significantly longer than a modern English mile, roughly 7.5 kilometers</note>: and thus the 12,000 stadia equal 257 1/7 such miles. In this manner, the length of this city is as great as the 21st part of the meridian <note>original: "Meridiani"</note> or the equator <note>original: "Æquatoris"</note>, and the same applies to its width and height. Nothing is mentioned regarding the height of the city in Ezekiel <note>referring to the vision in Ezekiel 40-48</note>, and its circumference is 18,000 measuring rods. Even one-seventh of the 12,000 stadia is larger than the length of the land itself in which Ezekiel’s city is located. What a great difference! Ezekiel’s city is seen earlier; the much larger city in Revelation <note>original: "Offenbarung"</note> appears afterward.

### Verse 21.

> And the twelve gates were twelve pearls, each of the gates was made of one pearl: and the square of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass.

¶ **Twelve gates)** verse 12.
¶ **Pearls)** Precious stones have their origin in the earth, whereas pearls originate in the water. The white luster of pearls and the yellow luster of gold play together beautifully. Compare verse 18.
¶ **Each of the gates was made of a single pearl)** Usually, a gate consists of two leaves <note>original: "Flügeln," literally "wings," referring to the two doors of a double gate</note>, but here each gate is a single whole piece, consisting of one pearl. These are twelve exceptional instruments <note>original: "Rüstzeuge," a term used for people chosen by God as "vessels" or tools for His work</note>, aside from those twelve apostles, who have been instrumental for a great multitude from among the Gentiles entering the Kingdom of **God**. Here Paul might well have his place, as well as Barnabas, Silas, Timothy, and others who performed special services for the entry of the Gentiles.
¶ **The square)** or, the street. Chapter 22:2. It is what one calls the marketplace in earthly cities. One enters onto such a square directly from the twelve gates.
¶ **Like transparent glass.** This is even more than just pure glass. Verse 18. The individual dwellings are surpassed in clarity by the public square.

### Verse 22.

And I saw no temple in it: for the **LORD**, **God**, the Almighty, is its temple, and the Lamb.

¶ **A temple**) Where there is a temple in a city, that temple is considered holier than the city outside its walls: but here the city is holy through and through. Now, it might be said that the city is a temple or seat of the **LORD**, compare verse 3 and Jeremiah 3:16–17, but it sounds even more glorious: **The LORD, God, the Almighty, is its temple, and the Lamb.** He also fills the new heaven and the new earth; He therefore surrounds the city, and sanctifies it, and all who are within it. He is all in all. 1 Corinthians 15:28.

¶ **And**) In this way, the same glorious <term>attributes</term> <note>original Latin: "Prædicata," referring to the titles or qualities ascribed to a subject</note> are assigned to **God** and to the Lamb. Verse 23, Chapter 22:1, 3, Chapter 7:10.

# And bring their— XXI. 25. 26.

¶ **Shall walk by the light of it**) In this way, the radiance of the city will extend outwards into the near and far distance. The nations are Israel’s companions.

¶ **The kings of the earth**) These words are limited and restricted by what follows—and there are many such modes of speech in Scripture. For example: **A wise son makes a glad father** (that is, if the father is still living); **A righteous man has regard for the life of his beast** (that is, if he actually owns livestock); Proverbs 10:1, 12:10. Thus, it is indicated here that the most glorious and worthy among the kings will bring such glory of theirs into the city.

¶ **Bring their glory into the same**) This is not an old-earthly majesty, but a majesty or glory befitting the <term>New Earth</term> <note>The biblical concept of a restored world following the final judgment</note> which the kings of the earth bring with them into the city; and this glory of theirs is elevated even further by being introduced into the city. Among the nations, magnificence <note>original: "Pracht"</note> is added to the glory. v. 26.

> And its gates shall not be shut by day: for there shall be no night there: 26 and they shall bring the glory and the magnificence of the nations into it.

¶ **Not shut**) so that the coming and going mentioned in verse 26 remains uninterrupted. Isaiah 60:11.

# XXI. 25. 26. And their—bring

¶ **Namely**) Gates are usually closed at night: and thus it is explained here why it mentions that there is no closing at night, and moreover, [it remains open] during the day.

¶ **There**) This is a restriction and limitation. *Chapter 22:5.* Outside the city, where the glory of God does not show itself so abundantly, there may well be a distinction between day and night. In the Lake of Fire, it is dark eternally. *v. 13.* The smoke <note>Referring to the "smoke of their torment" mentioned in Rev 14:11</note> will also contribute its part to this. *Chapter 14:11.*

**v. 26. They**) namely, those to whom it falls to do such a thing. *Isaiah 60:11.*

¶ **The glory and the magnificence of the nations**) The glory of the nations is promised to the holy city. *Isaiah 66:12.* and <term>wealth</term> <note>original Hebrew: "chel", meaning power, wealth, or a host</note>—the power or multitude of the heathens, *Isaiah 60:5, 15.* In the Book of Revelation, however, instead of "multitude," it says <term>honor</term> <note>original Greek: "ἡ τιμὴ" (hē timē)</note>, the <term>magnificence</term> <note>original Hebrew: "hadar", meaning splendor or majesty</note>, just as in *Isaiah 35:2* such glory (*Isaiah 60:13*) and magnificence are found together. Not all nations entirely, nor even all those who nevertheless walk by the light of Jerusalem, will enter; rather, only the most glorious and adorned procession of them.

### Verse 27.

**And there shall not enter into it anything common, nor whoever commits abomination and lies, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.**

¶ **And**) The wretched classes of such people who do not enter are recounted hereafter; here, however, it is only mentioned generally in the description of the gates, for whom these stand open or not.

¶ **Not**) Only the righteous will be there. *Isaiah 60:21.* Those who pass away without <term>repentance</term> <note>German: "Busse", a turning away from sin</note> and faith will not enter therein for all eternity.

¶ **Common**) <term>unholy</term> <note>original German: "gemeines", which in a biblical context refers to something "profane" or "ritually unclean" rather than just "ordinary"</note>. *Isaiah 52:1* says that into the holy city of Jerusalem no uncircumcised or unclean person shall enter anymore.

¶ **Lies**) "Committing lies" and "doing the truth" (*John 3:21*) are placed in opposition to each other. Whoever commits abomination and lies, and does not cleanse themselves from all defilement of the flesh and the spirit (*2 Corinthians 7:1*), has no fellowship with the Holy One, the True One. *Chapter 3:7; 6:10.*

¶ **Written**) *Chapter 20:15; Isaiah 4:3.* Blessed are these! Oh, if only we were there! Strive for it!

### Chapter XXII. 5. And there — Ages

¶ **No night** etc.) <note>original: "Reine Nacht 2c." refers to the biblical phrase "there shall be no night there."</note> What was touched upon in Chapter XXI:23–24 regarding how the radiance of the holy city would pour outward is summarized here, and it is indicated even more profoundly what kind of light the inhabitants themselves will enjoy.

¶ **Of a lamp**) At night, when the moon does not shine, or when one cannot see enough by its light, one lights lamps: but in Jerusalem they have no need for either the moon or lamps, nor even the sun.

¶ **Over them**) Chapter VII:15. Isaiah LX. <note>referring to Isaiah 60:19: "The sun shall no longer be your light by day, nor for brightness shall the moon give light to you; but the Lord will be to you an everlasting light."</note>

¶ **They shall reign**) When the inhabitants of the city are all rulers, where then are the subjects? They are outside the royal residence <note>original: "Redenz," likely a shortened form of "Residenz," the seat of government</note> on the new earth.

¶ **For the ages of ages**) <note>original: "In die ewigen Ewigkeiten," literally "into the eternal eternities."</note> This eternal reign is also testified to in Daniel VII:18, 27.

The divine wonder-mysteries are revealed to the believers bit by bit, and much must still happen before Jerusalem comes down from heaven. I recognize my own current interpretation as being very weak, and for that reason, it must be carefully observed whether this or that is presented as a firm doctrine, or merely for further reflection. In the main matter, I hope I am passing safely through the middle path between a far too literal and a far too free interpretation. Now, let everyone take a look with me at the holy city.

# And — must happen. XXII. 6.

The Kingdom of God has had to battle through much of the resistance described in this book; but the goal is precious. ## XX. 6. And — must happen

¶ **Certain and true**) They are true in themselves, and the saints can and should rely on them now and in the future. Compare Psalm 19:8–9 and consider how, in that passage, the Word of God is praised in such manifold ways—both for its own sake and in regard to those who love it.

¶ **The God of the spirits of the prophets**) The "spirit of prophecy" <term>prophecy: the inspired declaration of divine truth and future events</term> is mentioned in Chapter 19:10; but here it speaks of the *spirits of the prophets*. God is the God of glory, of love, of hope, of patience, of comfort, of all grace, and likewise the "God of the spirits of all flesh" (Numbers 16:22; 27:16); but here He is specifically the God of the *spirits of the prophets*. He works all things in them and brings them to completion (2 Peter 1:20–21). The angels are also spirits, and thus the prophets and their spirits have a similarity and an official kinship <note>original: "Amts-Verwandtschaft," meaning a connection based on their shared divine office or duty</note> with them. Through the spirits of the prophets, these things were prophesied from time to time long beforehand. Chapter 19:10. Both <note>referring to the angelic testimony and the prophetic tradition</note> confirm each other excellently: both types of testimony are from God. v. 9. It is the Lord whom the spirits of the prophets have as their God, and who has sent this angel with certain and true words.

# Behold, — of this book. XXII. 7.

¶ **His Angel**) This is the very same angel who is still speaking here, and who, in verse 16, is also called "his angel" by the **Lord Jesus**.

->The 7th Verse.<-

> Behold, I come quickly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.

¶ **Behold, I come quickly**) The same word, *quickly* <note>original Greek: ταχυ (tachy)</note>—meaning soon, or swiftly—is used here three times: in verses 7, 12, and 20. Thus, in this conclusion, the coming <term>coming: refers to the "Zukunft" or the Second Coming of Christ</term> of the **Lord Jesus** resounds with power. It is presented now not only as something near (as it was mentioned six times in Chapters 2 and 3), but for the seventh time, it is presented as something actual and certain. Compare Chapter 2:5 and see also verse 17 here.

¶ **Blessed**) in the coming of the **Lord**. **Jesus** continues the discourse here, as in verses 12–14.

¶ **Who keeps**) This "keeping" was already discussed in Chapter 1:3. Now, to this keeping is added the requirement that one should add nothing to these words, and take nothing away from them. See verses 18 and 19.

¶ **Of this book**) From this point on, it is very often called a *book*, as **John** has now almost completely finished writing it. In Chapter 1:3, he called it "the words of the prophecy," but not yet "the book." The **Lord Jesus** himself confirms the words of the prophecy of this book in verse 7, as does the angel in verses 9 and 10, and **John** himself in verses 18 and 19.

v. 9. **Your brothers**) The angel's fellow servants, and John’s brothers, are not only the prophets—of whom there were still some at that time—but also all those who keep this and every word of **GOD**.

# I—Morning Star. XXII. 16. [1047]

Uuu 4

2. David’s offspring at the time when Christ was born was not only in a very low state but also very few in number: so that it truly came down to Christ Himself. The lineage had so diminished, and is still so constituted, that Christ alone is the root and the offspring of David. Isaiah 11:1; 53:2. Amos 9:11. Sirach 47:25. # XXII. 17. And — Without Cost. [1048]

### The 17th Verse.

> And the Spirit and the bride say: Come. And let him that hears say: Come. And let him that is thirsty come: and whoever desires, let him take the water of life freely.

¶ And) In the preceding verses, **Jesus** testifies of His coming <note>The German 'Zukunft' refers to the Second Coming or Advent of Christ.</note>, and here He indicates that He is welcome.

¶ **The Spirit and the Bride say: Come**) The Bride is ready: The Bridegroom can come whenever He wishes: indeed, she desires and longs for it: she says, **Come**. The Spirit, who is given to her as a pledge <note>original: 'Pfand'; this refers to the theological concept of the Holy Spirit as a down payment or guarantee of future glory.</note>, speaks it for her. And this is not a twofold speaking, but the Spirit places it into the Bride's heart and mouth, and the Bride speaks it from the impulse of the Spirit. **Jesus** hears it: (**Romans 8:27**) He also approves of it: He says it here, and encourages others so that they should also say so, and learn to say it in this way.

2. But how can the Bride say, **Come**, when she herself comes down from heaven? Here the discourse concerns the Bride insofar as the saints on earth—who also belong to the holy city—await the **Lord Jesus** from heaven. **Philippians 3:20.**

3. Everything that the Spirit says to the churches in **Chapters 2 and 3** aims at the coming of **Christ**: and here, through the word **Come**, everything is summarily drawn together once more.

¶ **He who hears**) "He who has an ear, let him hear," was said so often in **Chapters 2 and 3**. But now the

### I testify — they are. XXII. 18. 19. <note>original: "Ich zeuge — ſind. XXII. 18. 19."; a reference to the closing warnings of the Book of Revelation against adding or removing words from the prophecy.</note>

Sharp warnings are not written there in vain: they must have a cause. Scholars write large books: but kings and princes condense great things tightly. In Revelation, the course of the world and of the Kingdom of God, from its inception until the end of all things and into eternity, is composed so vigorously and subtly that it fits entirely onto just a few small pages. Much becomes clear there, not necessarily from the words themselves, but from how they stand in relation to one another. Just as in a delicate watch the smallest flaw, not only in a tiny wheel but even in a single tooth of a gear, causes an inaccuracy: so too in this most remarkable little book of Revelation, the slightest addition or the slightest reduction can hinder its purposes in an often unexpected way. The heavenly <term>courtly style</term> <note>original: "Stilus curiæ"; referring to the formal, precise, and authoritative language used in a royal court, here applied to God’s sovereign communication.</note> has no equal. When one considers the glory of the <term>Author</term> <note>original: "Auctoris"; Latin for "author" or "originator."</note>, who is Jesus Christ and who places His own name at the very beginning, along with the importance of the content and the brevity of the speech in this prophetic, angelic, and indeed divine-royal manifesto, then one must recognize that very much must depend upon every single little word here. That is why God takes it so seriously.

2. In such matters, it is only right to take care that one does not become a hindrance to those who are doing worthy work on Revelation, as happens all too often.

# XXII. 20. He says—JE

->The 20th Verse<-

He who testified these things says: Yes, I am coming quickly: Amen, come Lord Jesus.

¶ (*He says*) Verse 17 and verse 20 are closely connected. The Spirit and the **Bride** <term>Braut</term> <note>In Christian theology, the "Bride" refers to the Church or the collective body of believers.</note> call out toward Jesus; John calls out; and the Lord answers: I am coming!

¶ *He who testified these things etc.*) This manner of speaking, *these things*, refers to the entire book. (Compare verse 6 and 18, and **John XXI. 24**). The one who testified is John, as the one who has seen and heard it (verse 8). This same word also applies to him in verse 18 and in a very specific way in **Chapter I. 2** and **John XXI. 24**. The Lord Jesus holds the name of the **faithful witness** <term>treuen Zeugen</term> in this book; however, the act of **witnessing** <term>Zeugen</term> or **giving testimony** <term>Zeugniß geben</term> is attributed to his servants.

2. What then does he say who witnesses this? For his part, he also says: come, Lord Jesus. But the Lord Jesus speaks in between and says: I am coming quickly. For such interrupted speeches occur with this word in **Acts I. 15** and specifically here: "Yes, I am coming" in **Chapter XVI. 15**. In contrast, it never says in this book: "he says, I come" without this specific context. The Lord Jesus puts "Yes" first, and John says "Amen." It is a lovely and beautifully expressed **simultaneous occurrence** <term>Simultaneum</term>! (Introduction § 19). "Come" and "I am coming" <note>original Latin: *Veni* & *Venio*</note> meet in a single moment. John has the inclination to say "come"; Jesus anticipates him and says "I am coming"; and the former then fully concludes: "Amen."

->Grace be with—all. XXII. 21.<-

3. **Yes, I am coming quickly**: this is the final word of Christ before his <term>Second Coming</term> <note>The original German uses *Zukunft*, which means "future" but in this theological context specifically refers to the *Parousia* or Advent of Christ.</note>. With this word, the prophecy of the Old Testament was also concluded in **Malachi 4:6**. However, the word "Come" is not placed there. A considerable amount of time was still to pass.

4. **Lord Jesus**, John adds. He knows Him who comes, and he knows his voice well.

5. John had a very particular reason to call out toward the coming of the Lord. **John 21:22**. He remained until the coming of the Lord; and when that coming dawned, his "remaining" was no more. He fell asleep in peace. However, he represents those saints who will be on earth at the time of Christ’s Second Coming. When the "I am coming" and the "come thou" reach their goal, the Lord will not delay for a single moment.

6. Three times in this conclusion it says, *I am coming*. The first and second times, a **blessing** <term>Seligkeit</term> <note>Often translated as "beatitude," referring to the "Blessed is he..." statements in verses 7 and 14.</note> is testified alongside it: verse 7 and 14. And at the third time, the blessing is actually found: for the one who comes is the **bright Morning Star**. Verse 16.

# Conclusion.

In such a manner, we have brought the interpretation of the **Revelation** <term>Offenbarung</term> <note>The Book of Revelation, also known as the Apocalypse.</note> to an end according to the order of the text. However, there are still one or two things remaining that could not be conveniently placed within individual passages, but rather belong to the overall consideration. Therefore, there follows here:

I. A **Chronological Table** <term>Zeit-Tafel</term>, in which the points of **prophecy** <term>Weissagung</term> and fulfillment are summarized.

II. A closer, yet modest, determination of the times of the **Beast**. <note>Referring to the "Beast" from Revelation 13 and 17, a central figure in the author's eschatological timeline.</note>

III. The characteristics of the true interpretation of this prophecy.

IV. An account of the waiting of people from one time to another.

V. A presentation of the effect of prophetic interpretations on the actions and omissions of mankind.

VI. An examination of several prophecies that are pointed out here and there.

VII. Several wholesome reminders.

XXXI. Yet it must also not set the end of the world too close after the flight of the angel with the **eternal Gospel** <note>original: *ewigen Evangelio*; a reference to the angel in Revelation 14:6 who proclaims the gospel to the world before the final judgment</note>.

XXXII. It must not create any arbitrary **proportion** <note>original: *Proportion*</note> in the prophetic numbers, but rather observe the one indicated in the text.

XXXIII. It must indicate a reason why no timeframes are expressed regarding the **bowls** <note>original: *Schalen*; the seven bowls of God's wrath described in Revelation 16</note>?

XXXIV. Likewise, why is the word **Angel** not expressed with every bowl, as it is with every **trumpet**?

XXXV. It must correctly compare the passages that require now **patience**, now **wisdom**, etc., and show them in their proper weight <note>referring to phrases in Revelation like "here is the patience of the saints" or "here is wisdom"</note>.

### XLII.
The aforementioned **calculation of time** <note>original: *Zeit-Rechnung*</note> begins only by refuting the most common errors, and it produces an inconspicuous prophetic month, year, day, and hour. From these, however, a beautiful **completeness** <term>original: *Rotundität*; referring to the mathematical "roundness" or internal harmony of the numbers</term> later emerges within the chronological periods actually present in the text, as does the **number seven** <note>a recurring biblical number signifying perfection or divine order</note>; and, when one holds these periods against one another, a wondrous proportion arises.

### XLIII.
The true interpretation walks a middle path, not only in the calculation of time but also in the subject matter itself. Where others interpret too much or too little of the text as referring to invisible or visible, or to past and future things, this interpretation instead takes everything together. It avoids the difficulties of those opinions that deviate to the right or the left, and it adopts the advantages arising from either side. It may take up everything that **Bossuet** <note>Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet (1627–1704), a French Catholic bishop who interpreted the Apocalypse as referring to the early Roman Empire</note> reproaches or wins against **Jurieu** <note>Pierre Jurieu (1637–1713), a Huguenot pastor who interpreted the Apocalypse as referring to the contemporary Papacy</note>, and likewise what **Abbadie** <note>Jacques Abbadie (1654–1727), a Protestant who critiqued Bossuet’s historical views</note> reproaches or wins against Bossuet—and whatever else turns into controversy between such interpreters—in no other way than to serve its own confirmation.

...to be won over to this opinion,) **Primasius** <note>a 6th-century bishop from North Africa</note> (who, besides the thousand years, also reckons the "three and a half times" <note>a prophetic period of 1,260 days or 3.5 years mentioned in Daniel and Revelation</note> from the beginning of the New Testament until the end of the world,) and among the Greeks, **Andrew of Caesarea** <note>original: *Andreas Cæsariensis*; a late 6th-century bishop whose commentary on Revelation became a standard reference for the Eastern Church</note>, who mentions the suffering of Christ here with more emphasis. **Scipione Maffei** <note>original: *Scipio Massejus*; an influential 18th-century Italian scholar and historian</note> adds the following to the words cited from **Cassiodorus**: <note>original: "*Quod subditur, spatium hoc multorum patrum sententia a nativitate Domini computari, ad opinionem multis olim subortam videtur referri, millesimo post Christum anno rerum universitatem dissolutum iri, & antichristum adventurum.*"</note> "Regarding what follows—that many Fathers believe this span of time should be calculated from the birth of the Lord—it seems to refer to an opinion that arose among many people long ago: that in the thousandth year after Christ, the universe would be dissolved and the **Antichrist** would arrive." Yet, as the year-count grew ever larger without any noticeable revolution, the literal meaning of the 1,000 years was allowed to prevail again, at the end of which the Antichrist would come.

26. The further one progressed with the calendar year, the more fitting it became to extend the interpretation of the prophetic times. Around the year 1200, Abbot Joachim <note>Joachim of Fiore (c. 1135–1202), a mystic who divided history into three ages corresponding to the Trinity</note> flourished; and as the date approached that would coincide with the 1,260 apocalyptic days <note>A reference to the 1,260 days mentioned in Revelation 11:3 and 12:6, often interpreted as years</note>, he and many others suspected a great upcoming change. He reinforced, in part, an error: namely, that the 1,260 days were taken to be as many years, and generally that one apocalyptic day was taken for one year. # History of Interpretations.

Regarding the year 1219. Matthias Flacius’s *Catalogue of the Witnesses of Truth* <note>original Latin: *Flacii catal. test. verit.*; Flacius was a Lutheran reformer who compiled historical evidence against the Papacy</note>, section 173; Johann Gerhard’s *Theological Commonplaces on the Final Judgment* <note>original: *Loc. de extr. jud.*</note>, section 78; and the appendix by Conrad Brüsske to Thomas Beverley’s *Chronological Register*, all summarized, yield the following. From ancient times, people added the Number of the Beast <note>the number 666 mentioned in Revelation 13:18</note> to the beginning of Muhammad’s reign <note>usually dated to the Hijra in 622 AD</note>. From the sum arising from 622 and 666, people became attentive to the year 1288. Around that same time, the Christians lost what they still held in Syria <note>referring to the fall of the final Crusader strongholds like Tripoli and Acre</note>, and people occupied themselves with a *Prognostication*: *Woe to the world in a hundred years* <note>original Latin: *Væ mundo in centum annis*</note>, **Woe to the world in a hundred years.** They therefore expected the greatest and final Antichristian misery, which would come to an end in *A. 1388*. When this came to nothing, they added another 100 years once or twice more, reaching the years 1588 and 1688, and also calculated the movements of the heavens for these dates. Finally, they abandoned this and no longer added the 666 years to Muhammad’s time, but rather to the year 1032, at which point they counted 1,000 years from the suffering of Jesus Christ. Therefore, they suspected the downfall of the Turks and the Papacy, and the expansion of Christianity throughout the whole world, would occur in the year 1698. *Lambert Daneau* <note>a French Reformed theologian</note> reversed it; he counted the 666 years from the suffering of Jesus Christ and then added the 1,000 years. See *On the Antichrist* <note>original: *de Antichr.*</note>, pages 98, 108. Compare *Dudley Fenner’s Theology*, page 172, published in the year 1589. Whether others chose to put the 666 or the 1,000 years first, at least toward the year 1666

### Conclusion, Part IV.

...there has been a great expectation. The treatise *On the Final Ruin of Rome* <note>original Latin: *De Romæ ruina finalis*</note> is entirely focused on this and gave Spizelius and Artopaeus cause for extensive deliberation.

35. Through the study of Scripture, people have once again come closer to the ancient truth. At the beginning of the last century, Johannes Piscator and others placed the Kingdom of the Beast and the Antichrist before those 1,000 years <note>referring to the Millennium, the thousand-year reign of Christ mentioned in Revelation 20</note>, and testified that not everything that should precede the end of all things has yet been fulfilled. Likewise, Daniel Cramer recognized in his annotated Bible <note>Cramer was a Lutheran theologian known for his "Glossed Bible"</note> that the thousand years (Chapter 20, verse 2) must only begin after the "Hallelujah" and after the victory in Chapter 19. However, he interpreted this as referring to the Peace of Religion <note>referring to the legal recognition of Protestantism in the Holy Roman Empire</note>, etc. (almost like Cotterius, Zeltner, and Mommers); and because he considered the end of the world to be very near, he extended the thousand years to hardly more than a man’s lifespan. In this, Franciscus Lambertus preceded him, and Zacharias Hogelius, Johannes Schindler, Nicolaus Mulerius, Johannes Brunsmann, and Melchior Knittelmayer did not distance themselves far from his view. The more natural this interpretation is, the more convincingly it proves that the connection between Chapters 19 and 20 was clear to these interpreters.

36. Afterward, through Cocceius <note>Johannes Cocceius, a Dutch theologian who developed Federal Theology</note>, a new diligence in this matter was brought about among many, although people allowed themselves to be led into many futile excesses with the "seven periods" <note>original Latin: *septem periodis*</note> or church ages.

### History of Interpretations.

37. A great door was opened by the dear Spener <note>Philipp Jakob Spener (1635–1705) was the founder of Pietism, a movement emphasizing individual piety and the "Hope for Better Times" for the Church</note>, who brought forth again what he and others called the "Hope for Better Times" <note>German: *Hoffnung besserer Zeiten*</note>. Although he set aside all specific details most cautiously—as was fitting for such a new beginning—he defended the main point with great earnestness, steadfastness, and certainty until his death. From then on, the truth in this matter has pressed forward ever more powerfully, though through many errors.

38. Those interpretations that now find the most approval are divided into three groups. I. Some interpret almost everything as the judgments upon the Jews, or even upon the Gentiles in the early times of the *New Testament*, and calculate the *1,000* years from the Ascension of Jesus Christ or from Constantine the Great. This is the opinion of *Grotius*, *Hammond*, of the *Apocalyptic Preliminaries* <note>original Latin: *Prænotionum apocalypticarum*</note>, etc., whereby the time periods are generally understood in the common sense <note>meaning literal days and years rather than prophetic symbolic time</note>. *Bossuet* <note>Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet, a prominent French bishop and theologian</note> takes this as a given and merely places the Antichrist shortly before the end of the world. II. Others still hold to the principle of a year for a day <note>the "year-day principle" where one prophetic day equals one calendar year</note> and to the *1,260*-year period. Those among them who let the Beast precede the thousand years set very different start and end dates for when the transition from the former to the latter should occur. *Joseph Mede* was one of the most prominent promoters of the *1,260*-year period, followed by *H. More*, *Pegamus*, and *Jurieu*...

26. He claimed he had received a command to raise an army of 144,000 men <note>A reference to the number of the "sealed" from the Book of Revelation 7:4.</note> to fight against the ungodly and the **Jansenists** <term>Jansenists: A Catholic theological movement, primarily in France, that emphasized original sin and divine grace; they were often persecuted by the crown and the Jesuits as heretics.</term>, whom he hated intensely. He asserted that King Louis XIV would command this army under the leadership of the angels **Gabriel**, **Michael**, **Raphael**, and **Uriel**. The Pope and the King of Spain were to meet King Louis in **Avignon**, and all princes and kings were to gather there to deliberate on how this great work could best be undertaken and completed. It was foretold that all Christians would return to the Roman Catholic Church; King Louis would overthrow and destroy the Turks and all **Muslims** <note>original: *Mahomedaner*</note> by sea and land, though more with spiritual than physical weapons. Despite these claims, he was allowed to keep his positions of honor and died in the year 1676.

# Examination of Recent Prophecies

§ 8. The fifteen kings are found from **Julius Caesar** <note>original: *Julio Cæfare*</note> up to **Hadrian** <note>original: *Adrianum*</note>, who takes his name from **Adria** or the **Adriatic Sea** <note>original: *Mari Adriatico*</note>. The three following were **Antoninus Pius**, **Antoninus Philosophus** <note>better known today as the Emperor-Philosopher Marcus Aurelius</note>, and **Lucius Verus**. It is quite possible that a poet—writing between the deaths of **Lucius Verus** and **Antoninus Philosophus**—turned history into a prophecy. This history recorded that **Antoninus Pius** became Emperor at a quite advanced age and yet reigned for a long time.

§ 9. **Rome** was founded in the year 3960 (not 3961) of the **Julian Period** <note>a chronological system used by scholars to reconcile different ancient calendars, starting in 4713 BCE</note> on October 29, as **Monsieur Des-Vignoles** <note>Alphonse des Vignoles (1649–1744), a French chronologist and clergyman</note> demonstrates in *Chronology, Volume II, page 865*. Starting from that date, one arrives at no significant conclusion using either the 948 years mentioned before, nor the 1836 years (should someone wish to add 888 years to the total, though I do not know why they would).

§ 10. However, if one wished to consider the 888 and the 948, or the 948 and the 888 (treating the 888 perhaps as a sign or a safeguard against the **third woe** <note>a reference to the apocalyptic "woes" described in the Biblical Book of Revelation</note>), then this would closely match the year 947 and the span of 888 5/6 years. These figures were derived entirely from other sources much earlier, as seen above on **pages 627 and 628**. Whether this is a mere coincidence, or where such an agreement might stem from, I do not know. Nor will I suggest how the sum of 948 and 888, counted from the birth of **Christ** and its true date, might point toward a specific end-goal for **Rome**. I build nothing upon it. <note>The author is expressing healthy skepticism about "numerology," the practice of finding mystical meaning in numbers</note>

## Prophecy of Saint Malachy, Archbishop, concerning the Supreme Pontiffs.

1 From a castle on the Tiber <note>original: "Ex castro Tiberis"; likely referring to the birthplace of Pope Celestine II, Città di Castello on the Tiber river</note>
2 The enemy expelled <note>original: "Inimicus expulsus"; referring to Pope Lucius II, whose family name Caccianemici literally means "to chase enemies"</note>
3 From the greatness of the mountain <note>original: "Ex magnitudine montis"; referring to Pope Eugenius III, who was born at Grammont</note>
4 The Abbot from Suburra <note>original: "Abbas Suburranus"; Pope Anastasius IV was from the Suburra district of Rome</note>
5 From the white countryside <note>original: "De rure albo"; Pope Adrian IV was born at St. Albans</note>
6 From a foul prison <note>original: "Ex tetro carcere"; the antipope Victor IV held the title of Cardinal of St. Nicholas in the Carcere—the prison</note>
7 The road across the Tiber <note>original: "Via Transtiberina"; the antipope Paschal III was the Cardinal of Santa Maria in Trastevere—literally "across the Tiber"</note>
8 From the Hungary of Tuscany <note>original: "De Pannonia Tusciæ"; the antipope Callixtus III was born in Hungary but served in Tuscany</note>
9 From the guardian goose <note>original: "Ex ansere custode"; Pope Alexander III's family coat of arms featured a goose</note>
10 Light in the entrance <note>original: "Lux in ostio"; Pope Lucius III was the Bishop of Ostia—*ostium* being the Latin word for entrance or mouth of a river</note>
11 A sow in a sieve <note>original: "Sus in cribro"; Pope Urban III's family name Crivelli means "sieve," and their family crest featured a sieve</note>
12 The sword of Lawrence <note>original: "Ensis Laurentii"; Pope Gregory VIII was the Cardinal of St. Lawrence and his coat of arms featured crossed swords</note>
13 He shall go forth from the school <note>original: "De schola exiet"; Pope Clement III was born in the Roman district of Schola</note>
14 From the cattle country <note>original: "De rure bovensi"; Pope Celestine III was of the Orsini family, but the motto refers to the Roman Boville—cattle—district</note>
15 A marked count <note>original: "Comes signatus"; Pope Innocent III was a Count of Segni—*signum* meaning sign or mark</note>
16 A Canon from the side <note>original: "Canonicus de latere"; Pope Honorius III was a Canon of St. John Lateran</note>
17 The bird of Ostia <note>original: "Avis Ostiensis"; Pope Gregory IX was the Bishop of Ostia and his coat of arms featured an eagle</note>
18 The Sabine Lion <note>original: "Leo Sabinus"; Pope Celestine IV was the Bishop of Sabina and his coat of arms featured a lion</note>
19 Count Lawrence <note>original: "Comes Laurentius"; Pope Innocent IV was a count and the Cardinal of St. Lawrence</note>
20 The sign of Ostia <note>original: "Signum Ostiense"; Pope Alexander IV was the Bishop of Ostia and a member of the Conti-Segni—*signum*—family</note>
21 Jerusalem of Campania <note>original: "Hierusalem Campaniæ"; Pope Urban IV was born in Troyes, Champagne, and had been the Patriarch of Jerusalem</note>
22 The crushed dragon <note>original: "Draco depressus"; Pope Clement IV’s coat of arms featured an eagle clutching a dragon</note>
23 The snakelike man <note>original: "Anguinus vir"; Pope Gregory X’s family coat of arms featured a snake</note>
24 A French preacher <note>original: "Concionator Gallus"; Pope Innocent V was born in France and belonged to the Order of Preachers, also known as the Dominicans</note>
25 The good count <note>original: "Bonus Comes"; Pope Adrian V's birth name was Ottobono—*bono* meaning good—and he was a count</note>
26 The Tuscan fisherman <note>original: "Piscator Thuscus"; Pope John XXI was a Tuscan and his name was Peter—traditionally the "Fisherman" apostle</note>
27 A composite rose <note>original: "Rosa composita"; Pope Nicholas III's coat of arms featured a rose</note>
28 From the custom-house of the lily-bearing Martin <note>original: "Ex teloneo liliacei Martini"; Pope Martin IV was treasurer—*telonearius*—of St. Martin of Tours and served in France, often symbolized by the lily</note>
29 From the leonine rose <note>original: "Ex rosa leonina"; Pope Honorius IV’s coat of arms featured a rose and lions</note>
30 A woodpecker among the morsels <note>original: "Picus inter escas"; Pope Nicholas IV was born in Ascoli—resembling *escas* or food—and Piceno—resembling *picus* or woodpecker</note>

63. From the Politian gridiron <note>original: "De craticula Politiana"; refers to Pope Pius IV, whose family was linked to the Medici of Florence (the city of the scholar Poliziano) and whose name was Angelo, though the "gridiron" likely references Saint Lawrence, a patron of the Medici</note>

§ 16. *Gabriel Bucelinus*, *Henricus Engelgrave*, *Cornelius à Lapide*, *Dionysius of Lützenburg*, *Johannes Palatius*, and many other Roman Catholics have considered these mottos, once they were published, to be the fruit of a prophetic spirit; to that extent, one can at least cite them *ad hominem* <note>Latin: "to the man"; an argument based on the opponent's own admitted principles.</note>. ### Examination of newer prophecies. 1153

...of Rome <note>referring back to the previous page's discussion on heraldry</note>, has provided a correct interpretation before others.

§ 20. However, one should carefully examine the mottos <term>mottos: *Devisen*, heraldic devices or short slogans associated with a coat of arms</term>, noting whether they are older or newer than Pope Gregory XIV and Arnold Wion <note>The Benedictine monk who first published the Malachy prophecies in 1595 in his book *Lignum Vitae*.</note>. The older ones correspond much more closely to the actual names of the men, their places of origin, etc. <note>original: "*zc.*", an abbreviation for *etc.*</note>, and consistently hit the mark. The newer ones, however, either cannot be satisfyingly resolved, or two different mottos seem to fit a single Pope—for example, in *Aymon* <note>referring to Jean Aymon, a French apostate and author</note>, both the 103rd and the 88th motto are applied to the name and coat of arms of Innocent XII—or they otherwise possess a greater vagueness <note>original: "*Laxitæt*"</note> and do not descend into specific details.

§ 21. For a long time before the Reformation, there were various people within the Roman Church who spoke of future things. Much of this can be found in Flacius’s *Catalog of the Witnesses of the Truth* <note>original: "*Flacii Catalogo testium veritatis*"; a work by Matthias Flacius Illyricus documenting pre-Lutheran dissenters</note>, in Wolfgang Lazius’s *Commentaries on the Prophecy of Methodius*, in Johannes Wolf’s *Memorable Events* <note>Latin: "*Memorabilibus*"</note>, in Gerhard’s *Catholic Confession* and *On the Last Judgment*, etc. To this also belongs the *Catastrophe of the World* <note>Latin: "*Catastrophe mundi*"</note> (London, 1683) and Jacques Massard’s *Harmony of Ancient Prophecies with Modern Ones*. In particular, the so-called *Burden of the Church* <term>original: "*Onus ecclesiæ*"</term>, which was compiled by Johannes, Bishop of Chiemsee <note>Berthold Pürstinger (1465–1543), who wrote under the name Johannes; his work was a sharp critique of church corruption</note>, in the year 1519 and reprinted several times, is a collection of such old prognostications <note>early forms of forecasting or prophecy</note>. However, much useless material is mixed in with them. Of this same sort is the work of Bernardino de’ Busti, in his *Lenten Sermons* <note>original catchword: "*drage-*", referring to *Quadragesimale*, a collection of sermons for the forty days of Lent.</note>

This corresponds exactly to the 106th motto: *Angelic Shepherd*; and the 107th, *Shepherd and Sailor* <note>Latin: *Pastor & nauta*</note>. What is claimed about such "fine Popes" relies mostly on the fact that their short descriptions have been interpreted as *moral archetypes* <term>moral archetypes: *characteres morales*, symbols of spiritual qualities or virtues rather than specific historical markers like names or heraldry</term>. § 26. The most recent point regarding the aforementioned mottos <term>mottos: *Devisen*, the prophetic phrases assigned to each pope</term> is ultimately the most useful: namely, their number. This number is 111 (§ 14), a very odd and unusual number. We submit for consideration whether it might not be based on the following circumstances:

(1) From the prophetic Word, the authors of the 111 mottos recognized that the worldly Papacy should last 666 years <note>A reference to the "Number of the Beast" from Revelation 13:18, often used in Reformation-era polemics to calculate the duration of the Roman Church</note>. This equals 111 *six-year periods* <note>Latin: *sexennia*</note>. One may compare the second part of this conclusion, § 12.

(2) From history, they observed that each Pope reigned for an average of 6 years (this was the case, for example, from the lifetime of *Ciacconius* <note>Alfonso Chacón (1540–1599), a scholar famous for his histories of the Popes and his work on the Malachy prophecy</note> back to the time of *Malachy*). Since they applied the proportion of the past to the future, they concluded that there would be 111 Popes within those 111 *six-year periods*.

(3) From older times, they possessed a *prognostication* <note>Latin: *prognosticum*</note> concerning the "Angelic Shepherd" <note>Latin: *pastore angelico*</note>, the "Shepherd and Sailor" <note>Latin: *pastore & nauta*</note>, etc. They then fitted the 111 Popes into these and other attached *symbols* <note>Latin: *symbola*</note>.

(4) The actual goal was to create a chronology of the newer Papacy: and

Often these objections wear each other down, yet they are of such a nature that, although individually they are quite easy to answer, they would exhaust anyone who attempted to address them all by their sheer number. Now, everything has been laid before everyone. Whoever wishes to ignore it, let them ignore it; whoever can grasp it, let them grasp it <note>original: *Wer es fassen kan, der fasse es*. This is a reference to the words of Jesus in Matthew 19:12.</note>.

How many important things, **Lord Jesus**, lie within your Revelation before your countenance, which I have passed by with my <term>dim eyes</term> <note>original: *blöden Augen*. In archaic German, "blöd" referred to weak or dim physical sight, rather than a lack of intelligence.</note>. Compensate for my deficiency, in myself and in others, out of your fullness.

# Appendix.

Because that which is reported regarding the still future <term>World-Ages<note>Refers to the "Ages of the World," a chronological system dividing history into epochs based on biblical prophecy.</note></term> in Chapter 20 and elsewhere might strike many readers as strange above all other things, it has been deemed useful to provide a translation here of the beautiful passage from <term>Vitringa<note>Campegius Vitringa (1659–1722) was a Dutch theologian and Hebraist whose "Anacrisis Apocalypseos" (1705) was a highly influential commentary on the Book of Revelation.</note></term>, in *Analysis of the Revelation* page 847 and following (which is further explained in *Ages of the World* page 355 and following).

Perhaps the great hope of the glorious future of the LORD—unto the complete redemption of His own and the general judgment which has been entrusted to Him by the Father—is aimed by us at too long a distance? I confess it: it is postponed longer than the common man in the Christian church imagines. And I myself do not write of this matter without a sense of anxiety, although I do not particularly need to fear in the bright light of the truth. <margin>*</margin> I love the appearing of the Lord JESUS, and I do not pray for a delay of the end, in the hope that I shall find mercy on 그 day. Yet I hold it to be in accordance with faith and prudence that one leaves room for God to complete His work on earth before He brings an end to the <term>Ages<note>original Latin: "Seculis"; refers to the distinct epochs of time or world-eras.</note></term>: and we should not, in a masterless <note>meaning: "presumptuous" or "undisciplined"</note> manner, presume to set the times of the world and the church according to our own pleasure; for this, as the Lord has taught us, belongs to God alone. <note>Acts 1:7: "He said to them: 'It is not for you to know the times or dates the Father has set by his own authority.'"</note> For the work which God [performs] on earth...

<summary>This appendix introduces a translation of the theologian Vitringa to address potential reader confusion regarding the timing of the "World-Ages" and the Second Coming. Vitringa argues that while the end may seem delayed, Christians must patiently allow God to complete His earthly work according to His own schedule.</summary>

[...decided] to represent, and for whose representation He created the <term>Ages<note>original: "Secula." A Latin term used by theologians to describe the great epochs or eras of history through which God’s plan for humanity unfolds.</note></term>, is great, astonishing, and wondrous; it is our duty to measure this not according to our own lowly minds, but according to the divine majesty, greatness, and the breadth and depth of His <term>counsels<note>original: "Rathschläge." This refers to God's pre-ordained plans or decrees.</note></term>. For it is a sign of our meager spirit to confine the specific times, which **GOD** has dedicated to carrying out His counsels, within narrow bounds. Moreover, it is a sign of impatience and unbelief to run ahead of those times with our own thoughts and to say, with the <note>In the 18th century, "carnal" was often used to describe a literal or worldly understanding of scripture, as opposed to a "spiritual" or enlightened one.</note>carnal Jews: *Let Him make speed and hasten His work, that we may see it:* Isaiah 5. On the other hand, it is the nature of faith and sobriety [to] not hasten. Isaiah 28:16. For by this one knows that **GOD**, though it may seem He delays, yet truly does not tarry,
->but does everything beautifully in<-
->His own time.<-

# Catalog
->of several books which the Erhard<-
->Bookstore in Stuttgart has partly printed at its own expense,<-
->and partly are available there in<-
->abundance.<-

**Bengel, J. A.** sixty edifying sermons on the Revelation of John, or rather of Jesus Christ, including a supplementary collection of similar content. Both are woven together so that it may be regarded either as a second part of the explained Revelation, or on its own as a strengthened testimony of the truth. Along with a useful guide on how these sermons may be read throughout the church year as a <term>postil<note>original: "Postille." A book of sermons or commentaries arranged according to the church calendar to be read during worship or private study.</note></term>, new edition. <term>Octavo<note>original: "8." A standard book size of the era, where each sheet of paper is folded into eight leaves.</note></term>. 1771.

—— **World Ages**, in which the scriptural timeline is proven, and the seventy weeks <note>A reference to the prophecy in the Book of Daniel.</note>, along with other important texts and salutary teachings, are explained. Octavo. 1746.

—— **Outlines** of the four books of the New Testament, namely 1.) the Evangelists, 2.) the Acts of the Apostles, 3.) the Apostolic Epistles, and 4.) the Holy Revelation. Octavo. 1742.

**Reliable Account** of the life, death, and writings of the late <note>original: "weiland." An archaic term meaning "of former times" or "deceased."</note> Dr. Johann Albrecht Bengel; together with a memorial of love, composed by Johann Philipp Fresenius. Octavo.

**Rieger, G. C.** The right and easy way to heaven through eight steps of the Beatitudes; previously presented to the Lord’s congregation in public sermons from Christ’s Sermon on the Mount from Matthew 5:1–12, but now published along with the biography of the late author and a list of his writings printed before and after his death, by <term>M. W. J. J. Cless<note>"M." stands for Magister, a master's degree often held by clergy.</note></term>. Octavo. 1754.

**Storren, Joh. Christ.** The Following of Christ, presented in seven sermons on the usual Gospel for the feast of St. Andrew, from Matthew 4:18–22. Octavo. 1755.

—— The Kingdom of Heaven under the image of the ten virgins, from Matthew 25:1–13, in 18 sermons.
